newsitem.title: USA: St Paul completes reinsurance transaction.
newsitem.headline: St Paul completes reinsurance transaction.

text.p: St. Paul Cos Inc said Monday it had completed with Goldman, Sachs & Co a $68.5 million securitized reinsurance transaction.
St. Paul said the transaction will provide its reinsurance operation, St. Paul Re, with additional reinsurance capacity for up to 10 years.

St. Paul said the proceeds from the transaction, raised in a private placement, will fund a single-purpose reinsurance company, George Town Re. It said this will allow St. Paul Re to tap into dedicated financial capacity to write new business without having to seek additional capital and without any impact on St. Paul Cos' balance sheet.
The company said St. Paul Re will cede reinsurance business from certain lines on a proportional basis to George Town Re under a 10-year reinsurance treaty.
St. Paul Cos said George Town Re has issued two types of securities to investors -- notes and preference shares.
The notes mature in 10 years. Interest payments on them will depend on the performance of the reinsurance business ceded by St. Paul Re and investments.
It said $44.5 million was raised through these notes, of which $23.2 million was invested in zero-coupon securities.

Dividends and the redemption value of the preference shares, redeemable in the year 2000, are also based on the performance of the ceded business. The company said it raised $24 million in preference shares.
A total of $45 million from the two securities will be used as collateral for the reinsurance provided to St. Paul Re.
St. Paul Cos provides property-liability insurance and services.
The company said this transaction was the first major one executed by Goldman Sach's Insurance Products Group.
